method_note: Cuts carry 4,113-12,489 enumerated crossings, so iterative escape-banning cannot converge; the one-shot cut ban is the only construction that provably forces a specific crossing. Four of the twelve edges cannot be tested this way at all: the dout net (qb -> MCU exit X10Y4) must re-cross the same cut and cannot share the single legal crossing (RMUX08@12,4->RMUX32@14,4; RMUX09@14,4->RMUX28@14,8; RMUX69@14,6->RMUX76@14,10; RMUX74@11,4->RMUX08@12,4). One more (RMUX68@9,4->RMUX74@11,4) failed to route under the ban.
observed: Five other catalogued edges were forced by the same one-shot full-cut construction and each read STUCK (49/0). MATCHED SIBLING CONTROLS -- identical cut ban, identical qa/qb placement, identical destination node, but keeping a DIFFERENT non-catalogued feeder as the single legal crossing -- were built for four of them (RMUX15@2,4->RMUX68@6,4; RMUX21@14,9->RMUX87@14,5; RMUX33@17,4->RMUX39@14,4; RMUX80@15,8->RMUX33@15,4) and ALL FOUR ALSO READ STUCK.
scope: RETAINED NEGATIVE about METHOD, not about silicon: a full-cut forced construction (4.8k-19.2k banned edges) does not generally yield a functioning image, so a STUCK reading from it is UNINTERPRETABLE and is not evidence that any edge fails to conduct. The five STUCK targets (RMUX15@3,4->RMUX68@6,4; RMUX21@14,8->RMUX87@14,5; RMUX21@14,9->RMUX87@14,7; RMUX33@15,4->RMUX39@14,4; RMUX80@15,7->RMUX33@15,4) therefore remain UNVERIFIED, exactly as before this campaign -- neither proven dead nor admitted. Positive readings from the same construction remain valid (a toggling signal is self-validating), which is how RMUX87@14,8->RMUX68@14,7 was admitted. This independently reproduces the 2026-08-13 reframe: heavily constrained/congested constructions fail for reasons unrelated to per-edge conduction.

method_note: Fixing this required two workbench corrections that also invalidate any earlier same-shaped analysis: (1) routed-JSON wire names are inconsistently zero-padded ('X12Y4_RMUX08' from the pad flow vs 'X14Y10_RMUX21' from the relay flow), so hop comparison must normalize the resource index -- comparing raw strings silently missed real witnesses on every edge whose index has a leading zero; (2) the workbench arch's BRAM routing-pip loader did not consult the edge blacklist, so a 'forced' route could escape a geometric cut through the BRAM column's TMUX->KMUX->InputMUX chain, which jumps eight tiles in one hop. Both are fixed.
observed: The unconstrained-readback method (pad witness) resolves the structural limit of the MCU-dout witness: because the pad sits on the same side of the cut as the relay register, the readback never crosses the cut, so the build stays lightly constrained. Two previously untestable edges were closed positively this way. A third, RMUX68@9,4->RMUX74@11,4 (image 92a3551052022b59caa59ee317dfe6025830d221c2677658a4d0903c9c1e39a4), read STATIC HIGH 200/0 -- but its MATCHED SIBLING control (same cut ban, same placement, same destination, keeping RMUX68@8,4->RMUX74@11,4 instead; image ce5e7d6920137d52dcfc4fc6e5c10409e9fe48fe88acebcd8595b41d4f18c095) ALSO read STATIC HIGH 200/0, so that verdict is uninterpretable and the edge stays gated as unverified. RMUX09@14,4->RMUX28@14,8 and RMUX69@14,6->RMUX76@14,10 fail to route at all once the cut ban is fully honoured.
